stemBlocks.value: The quadratic function g is defined by g(x) = -x² + 6x + 7. (a) Express g(x) in the form a(x + h)² + k, where a, h and k are constants. (b) Hence state the coordinates of the maximum point of g. (c) Write down the equation of the line of symmetry of the graph of g.
Think first: Factor the -1 out of the x terms first — completing the square inside a negative bracket is where most marks are lost.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p154-q02 from workbook page 154.

solutionSteps.instruction: Complete the square inside the bracket.

contentBlocks.value: Half of -6 is -3, and (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9, so x² − 6x = (x − 3)² − 9
-(x − 3)² is never positive and equals 0 when x = 3, so the greatest value of g is 16
The vertical line through the vertex

strategyBlocks.value: Take -1 out of the x² and x terms, complete the square inside the bracket, expand the -1 back through and read off the vertex.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) g(x) = -(x − 3)² + 16, so a = -1, h = -3 and k = 16  (b) Maximum point (3, 16)  (c) Line of symmetry x = 3.

whyThisWorks.value: With a negative leading coefficient the squared bracket is subtracted, so the expression is largest when the bracket is zero — the turning point becomes a maximum instead of a minimum. Factoring the -1 out before completing the square keeps the inside a standard x² − 6x, and multiplying back through at the end is what converts the -9 into +9. The vertex form then displays the maximum value and its position at a glance.

commonErrors.misconception: Failing to multiply the -9 by the factored -1, giving -(x − 3)² − 2.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Failing to multiply the -9 by the factored -1, giving -(x − 3)² − 2.

commonErrors.misconception: Halving 6 to get +3 but forgetting the sign change caused by the factored -1.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Halving 6 to get +3 but forgetting the sign change caused by the factored -1.

commonErrors.misconception: Calling (3, 16) a minimum because the constant k is positive.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Calling (3, 16) a minimum because the constant k is positive.

examTip.value: After completing the square with a negative leading coefficient, expand your answer back out — this is the single most common place to lose a sign.
